checks.evidence: lesson.mdx:1 — "A numeric sample array becomes a signal only when its index, units, sample period, and acquisition assumptions are stated."
checks.judgment: The first paragraph is the exact course.yaml opening and states the lesson's problem declaratively.

checks.evidence: lesson.mdx:9-11 begins with the literal buffer c=[0,1,0,-1,0,1,0,-1] before the first Definition at line 25.
checks.judgment: The first formal definition names distinctions already exposed by the concrete record and figure.

checks.evidence: The five content headings move from record metadata to time, rate, calibration, and finite-domain assumptions.
checks.judgment: Every section serves the single goal of analyzing a measured waveform under explicit index, time, amplitude, rate, and acquisition contracts.

checks.evidence: 2,859 counted words after component stripping, five content sections, two definitions, one worked example, one paired in-body exercise, six closing exercises, and four substantive figures.
checks.judgment: The derivations, boundary cases, and complete solutions support the declared 32-minute estimate and the 30-40 minute core target.

checks.evidence: The definitions state domains and units precisely; the Example computes both rate interpretations; the clipping boundary is honestly a Remark.
checks.judgment: No theorem dressing or incomplete proof environment appears.

checks.evidence: Exercises produce ledgers, boundary judgments, incompatible interpolants, a dimensional derivation, representation choices, and an impulse decomposition; the in-body axis-repair task is parallel to the rate/calibration example.
checks.judgment: The work is native DSP/mathematical production rather than recognition or transplanted arithmetic.

checks.evidence: course.yaml lists no prerequisite for sampled-sequences.
checks.judgment: Earlier-lesson retrieval is not applicable to the first course lesson.

checks.evidence: All seven Exercise blocks contain Solution blocks; the boundary, interpolation, energy, plotting, and impulse solutions show their derivations and end with the transferable move.
checks.judgment: No solution is answer-only, omitted, or trick-dependent.

checks.evidence: The closing set has one mechanical warm-up, the four-row time/code/voltage ledger; the remaining five require boundary analysis, refutation, derivation, strategy choice, or transfer.
checks.judgment: The mechanical-item cap is met.

checks.evidence: Boundary probe: empty/one-sample/constant records. False claim: connected sample dots. Skipped derivation: rate scaling of physical energy and power.
checks.judgment: The set carries three E6 categories, exceeding the required two.

checks.evidence: Exactly one closing exercise decomposes x=[2,-1,0,3] into shifted impulses, and its solution links once to <Ref lesson="impulse-response-and-convolution">.
checks.judgment: There is exactly one forward bridge and its solution names the next lesson's linearity, time invariance, and convolution connection.

checks.evidence: lesson.mdx:81-83 — "n counts samples and has no unit; nT_s locates a sample in physical time..."; lines 180-182 — "A line joining sample markers is a display or reconstruction choice..."
checks.judgment: Both KeyFacts restate claims already stated explicitly in the immediately preceding definition/prose and figures. Deleting either loses no boundary, synthesis, or forward consequence, so both fail the required callout deletion test.

checks.evidence: lesson.mdx:17 — "Lyons begins discrete-time DSP with this separation"; line 140 — "Orfanidis separates this path...; Smith likewise treats the array..."
checks.judgment: These inline secondary-source pointers narrate compilation provenance without buying a distinct proof, stronger claim, notation origin, or checkable primary artifact.

checks.evidence: No instances of "does the work", "recreated below", "under the hood", or equivalent narration occur.
checks.judgment: The prose states the operation and consequence directly.

checks.evidence: Captions claim respectively that samples omit the path, contract fields are separate, rate rescales time/frequency, and calibration cannot undo clipping.
checks.judgment: Each visual carries one pedagogical claim; captions state takeaways rather than describe decoration, and alt text identifies the relevant geometry and values.

checks.evidence: course.yaml sets demo: null.
checks.judgment: No demo is required for this lesson's static representation distinctions.

checks.judgment: No run exceeds the cadence limit in a materially dense region.

checks.judgment: The fold-stripped skeleton reconstructs the argument.

checks.evidence: Bold is confined to defined terms and run-in labels, italics mark source titles, code formatting marks no prose emphasis, and four em dashes over 2,859 words are below the heuristic ceiling.
checks.judgment: Typed emphasis and punctuation remain disciplined.

checks.evidence: The lesson uses declarative engineering prose and second person only in tasks such as "Construct", "Name", and "check".
checks.judgment: No rhetorical question, teaser, invented persona, exclamation, or chatty aside appears.

checks.judgment: The bibliography is real, relevant, and chapter/lesson precise; the defect is inline use, not reference specificity.

required_fixes.action: Remove the two tautological KeyFacts or rewrite each to add information absent from the surrounding body. For the n/nT_s callout, add an operational boundary such as the impossibility of aligning unlike-rate records by index alone. For the connected-dots callout, add the exact acquisition/reconstruction condition that licenses a curve or a forward consequence for later sampling theory. Do not leave either as a restatement.

Rewrite the three secondary-source scaffolding sentences so the DSP facts are the grammatical subjects, and leave Lyons, Orfanidis, and Smith in the chapter-precise References only. Retain an inline Schaedler link only if it explicitly sends the reader to the checkable competing-path visualization; otherwise move it to References as well.
